correctness.rationale: Complete explicit graph and 120-element automorphism group verified by oriented-triangle propagation; all 5,887 matching faces enumerated. Five complete mod-two simplicial boundary ranks (29,286,1114,1357,125), together with exact chain-complex upper bounds and rational rank >= mod-two rank, force rational homology concentrated in degree three of rank 64. Signed Lefschetz formula with reduced augmentation yields the entire 120-element character and its antipodal trace 16. Exact finite-group character inner products give multiplicity triples (2,4,2) and (2,2,1) for rational A5 irreducibles of dimensions 4,5,6. The executable checks 2,775,600 signed equivariance incidences and all identities and gives independent reproducible exact input and output. Rational orbit cohomology follows by averaging; no unjustified integral or infinite conclusion is drawn.

evidence: Shareshian–Wachs (arXiv:math/0409054), introduction and general results, concern complete graph and chessboard matching complexes and natural symmetric-group modules.

Bate–Everitt–Ford–Ramos (arXiv:2312.13750), accepted manuscript introduction and Section 1.1, explicitly focus their fixed-parameter matching-complex homology calculation on complete hypergraphs and their full symmetric groups.
Bayer–Jelić Milutinović–Vega (arXiv:2411.04601), Theorem 2, is restricted to outerplanar graphs.
broader_coverage.reasoning: None of the broader theorems computes the action on the subcomplex of matchings restricted to the noncomplete icosahedral graph. Restricting an \(S_{12}\)-module for the complete graph does not determine homology of a proper noninvariant graph-edge subcomplex. The family of fibre-closed complexes in the 2023 source supplies asymptotic representations rather than this object-specific 120-element character. The icosahedron is planar but not outerplanar.

originality.rationale: The closest identical-object icosahedral result determines only a nonequivariant integral homotopy decomposition. Its homology rank 64 does not imply any homological character of the full group. The newly computed complete character, antipodal decomposition 40+24, and quotient invariants are not supplied by the inspected exact-object or broad complete-graph/outerplanar/complete-hypergraph sources. Actual published-finding corpus searches of equivalent formulations and parent theorems found no covering claim; unindexed equivalents remain a residual risk.
residual_risks: Index coverage is not a proof of unique publication priority; unindexed exact equivariant computations could exist.
The publicly available same-graph result determines integral homotopy type, but no natural equivariant model is provided; the new complete character is independently computed.
This rational representation does not determine the action on \(\mathbb Z/3\) torsion or the integral group-module lattice.

value.rationale: The icosahedral matching complex is a natural, previously studied torsion-bearing planar example with exceptional full A5×C2 symmetry. The complete rational module resolves a genuine missing symmetry-sensitive invariant, distinguishing antipodal-even 40-dimensional and antipodal-odd 24-dimensional homology and proving vanishing of rotation-invariant homology and of higher rational orbit-space cohomology. Nonequivariant homotopy and Betti-number data cannot supply these conclusions, so the result is not a routine recomputation.
